text: When I arrive at the café, I immediately received a rest day notice from Reina, which said I would have tomorrow off.
Me joining the café has helped lighten the workload for the whole team, and everyone can have rotating days off. For example, A-37 is off today.
The thing is, A-37 comes and goes like a ninja. I can barely keep track of where he is or what he's doing, though it's probably not that important.
I, on the other hand, have something important to do today.
Remembering the lovely afternoon tea to which Saturne had invited me, I think it's about time to return the favor. That's why I intend to treat him to his favorite sparkling orange.

Seeing as we still have a bit of time before the rush starts, I asked Reina how to make it, but it's a bit more complicated than I thought... There's actually a secret Éternité recipe! Reina smiles playfully at my somewhat amazed expression.
I take back what I said earlier, about "there's nothing special being added to Éternité's ice water". It seems like that A-37 might actually come to get ice water.

When the café's pretty empty, Reina doesn't usually ask too much about what we're doing. As she says herself, as long as we fulfill our responsibilities, then occasionally loafing around can actually make the job more fun. So after cleaning up, I take some ice-cold sparkling water over to Saturne.
Saturne seems a little surprised when I turn up at his house.
I follow Saturne to the usual spot, only to unexpectedly discover a Mahjong table where the dining table had been before! By the looks of things, a game had only just ended.

I've actually heard of this "Which tile to discard" game. Usually there are several different choices when it comes to the endgame, and everyone chooses different tactics depending on their own understanding of the game. A lot of the time, a group will even discuss which playstyle is the safest to adopt.
He nods to me, and I knowingly draw a tile from the wall. It's the 5-Sou.
I consider the current situation as if it were me.

Following Saturne's reminder, I recall the reason for my visit today, and carefully recount what I know about the Four Great Jyanshis. Seeing as he's just mentioned it, I also tell him about the Mahjong Soul Shrine tournament.
Saturne listens to me carefully, while at the same time tapping the table with the knuckle of his middle finger and muttering something under his breath.
Thinking of Ichihime's personality, it really is hard to imagine her running such an important tournament.

That being said, when I think about it, Ichihime single-handedly keeps the Mahjong Soul Shrine immaculate. While in some things she can be a little ditzy, with the help of Wanjirou she has managed the shrine perfectly for many years, never failing to hold special occasions and celebrations of all sizes.
Ichihime's real ability is always overlooked, thanks to her appetite and tendency to go for All Simples.
Saturne is silent for a moment, before mumbling to himself.
I see Saturne's smile fade, as if he's imitating his friend's tone, but he quickly gives up and waves to me.
From what I know of A-37, if it wasn't a perfect imitation then it's at least 80% accurate.
Is A-37 interesting? This is a debatable question, as it depends on which aspect... From simply a conversational perspective, he really is a man of few words.
Saturne smiles at me, his eyes obscured by the sunlight reflecting off his glasses.

Following Saturne's reminder, I recall the reason for my visit today, and carefully recount what I know about the Four Great Jyanshis. Saturne listens to me carefully, while at the same time tapping the table with the knuckle of this middle finger as if pondering something.
I can almost see Saturne's gossipy soul blazing away, but who could reject the truth if it's right in front of them?

The address I got from Wanjirou is still burning a hole in my pocket. After sleeping on it, I've decided not to rush to give it to Eve, as I've started having a few doubts about Lily. In particular, why, over so many years, has she never contacted Eve?

The questions that had arisen during my sleepless night keep popping into my head, one after another... But then I recall the glow in Eve's eyes when she spoke about Lily, and that's not something you can fake. I'm lying against the cat tree, lost in thought, when I'm startled by a face popping into view. It's Ichihime.
I look at the cookies in Ichihime's hand, then shake my head.
I heave a sigh and, considering Ichihime's recent diet, take three of the cookies.
I don't really agree with this idea. Just now, however, Reina and Momo came by, so maybe I should ask their opinions.
Momo carefully moves a chair next to me, then plants a heavy kiss right on my forehead.
Momo's tender tone also serves as a reminder. Worrying is never as good as seeing with my own eyes. After all, seeing is believing.
Reina has a point. If I think about it, the very fact that Eve came all the way to One Han City by herself to look for Lily shows that she's made of stronger stuff than I give her credit for.
But I just can't bear to see people around me upset...
I consider it again and again, and still think that Reina is right. Eve is a responsible adult. If I really have concerns, I can ask to go with her.
I feel much lighter after thinking it through. I work quicker too, and the cleaning's finished before I know it.
Gentle chiming announces Eve's promised arrival, who comes in and gives me a big hug.
I don't know whether to laugh or cry at the good news. After all, I've been worrying myself sick the whole morning for nothing!
Eve looks a little downcast. She gently shakes the ice water that Reina handed her, and I hear the crisp chink of ice cubes hitting the wall of the cup.
Eve looks up at me before quickly dropping her gaze. It's easy to tell how she's feeling, as it's written all over her face.
I said nothing, but sat next to her in companionable silence. Maybe it was the catharsis of speaking her mind, but it seems like Eve speaks more lightly.

Eve, like anyone who believes they will one day meet long-departed friends once again, has imagined all sorts of possibilities for Lily. I don't know her at all, so I am not in a position to offer an opinion, but even now I'm willing to go along with Eve's guesses.
Because only then can they one day be reconciled.
Eve hesitates briefly before continuing.

Faced with Eve's request, I think it's impossible to explain just how difficult it must have been for Lily Kitahara to rely on her Mahjong talent not just to win, but to become one of the Four Great Jyanshis. But I suppose you never know if you don't try, right? And besides, maybe Eve is a secret Mahjong genius too!
Just as Eve and I are about to draw up a Mahjong training program for her, Ichihime comes over with two iced lattes.
I fish out the scrap of paper with Lily's address on it and hand it to Eve.

Whichever way I look at it, I think Momo is right. Rather than just sitting here in anxious indecision, I'd better go and see for myself what sort of person this Lily Kitahara is. While I can't make Eve's mind up for her, I might as well do whatever I can.

When the café's pretty empty, Reina doesn't usually ask too much about what we're doing. As she says herself, as long as we fulfill our responsibilities, then occasionally loafing around can actually make the job more fun. So in the calm before the rush hour, I ask for some time off and head for the subway. My destination: the convent.

While St. Severus's is nominally in the northern suburbs, it's actually not that far from the city, with lively communities, shopping areas and even schools nearby. Factoring in subway transfers, the trip should take between 40 and 50 minutes.
I approach the entrance, only to be stopped by a nearby monk. His expression is far from friendly, and he looks at me like I'm some kind of scoundrel.

My impression of monks is that they are kind, peaceful people, who rarely have such vicious expressions. I think for a minute, but realize that it's my first time here, so I'm unlikely to have offended anyone. Best be polite and ask what's up.

The monk is pretty firm, and there seemed to be no room for any negotiation. I don't think I'll be getting inside today, and there's nothing for me to do but head back. I don't even know if Eve will be able to see Lily if it's like this when she comes.
As I leave, however, I hear the monk grumbling faintly.
It seems I'm not the only one who's come looking for Lily. I wonder who else it might be. Could Eve have already found Lily here?
Also, what did he mean by heathens scheming against the Four Great Jyanshis? The legend of the Four Greats, which I thought was becoming clearer, seems to be getting shrouded in yet more mysteries.

Thanks to my unsuccessful trip, I arrive back at the café a lot earlier than I had planned... Only to see Eve is already inside, surrounded by Reina and the others. She's holding a notebook, and studiously jotting things down.
She seems happy to see me come in, and gives me a friendly wave.
I lower my head and, taking the pen from Momo, write the word "All Simples" in the notebook. I notice that she's watching and taking her own notes at the same time.
I quietly move aside and watch the young women intensely discussing Mahjong strategies, while Eve and Momo take notes.
It's not until the first wave of rush hour guests arrive that they stop talking and start working.
I look at Eve, mention briefly about going to the convent but failing to see Lily, then give her the piece of paper with the address on it.

Saturne's words reminded me of the sparkling orange by my side. I take it out quickly, and count myself lucky that the scorching temperature hasn't affected the insulating bag. Tiny drops of water condense on the outside of the bottle when it meets the warm outside air.

Seeing this, Saturne claps his hands and asks the butler who was standing close by to take it, who then uses a napkin to wipe away the water droplets on the bottle and hands it back to me. I can't recall ever seeing a butler in attendance the previous times, so can't help but look at him a few more times.

I see two empty bottles on a wooden tray, itself placed atop a metal shelf behind the butler. I can't be certain how far away they are, but their shapes are similar to that of the sparkling orange bottle in my hand.
In order to maintain its unique charm, most things in Éternité are custom-made, including this bottle, which was carefully designed by Reina's uncle. In a flash, Hinata's words pop into my head.
Could A-37 have come here? But he clearly refused to make deliveries here! As if sensing my wandering thoughts, Saturne calls out to me solicitously.
I didn't tell Saturne the real reason, and anyway it's all conjecture at present. Even if they do know each other, it wouldn't be polite to directly ask about their relationship.
Saturne said this very earnestly. While I don't know what his interpersonal relationships are like, I do know that there are often things that powerful people have to do, whether they like it or not.
Perhaps I seem harmless to him, seeing as I'm not part of any faction, or someone that he needs to be wary of. Maybe I should visit him more often.
I smile and nod, taking my leave as he watches me depart.
I feel a stab of concern when I get home and see the dark loft, so hurriedly go up.
No words of farewell, nor mention of a return. As soon as I see the money neatly arranged on the table in the loft, I just know. A-37 is gone.
I pick the money up and have a look. If I'm not mistaken, this should be his salary for the time he worked at Éternité.

The more I think about it where A-37 might go, the more I realize how little I actually know about him. He's like a mysterious traveler, erasing all traces of his own existence. Just like how he left his bed—without even a crease, as if no one had ever slept in it.
I seal the money in an envelope and put it in the drawer of his bedside table. I think he'll be back. I can't say when, but I know that bonds between people are not so easily broken.
Eve lowers her head, stroking the back of the note with her thumb. When she finally looks up, thanking me softly, I see her eyes are a little red.
{character:Eve Krist} I'm so thankful to have met you, {var:player_nickname}!
As if aware that her brimming eyes are about to spill over, Eve turns away and vigorously wipes away her tears. When she turns back, she's the cheerful and handsome woman I first met.

While Eve and Lily didn't have the joyful reunion and return home that I was hoping for, from what Eve was saying I think she'll be staying in One Han City for a while. I hope it's long enough for them to patch things up... And long enough for us to become good friends.
No, that's not quite right, seeing as we're already friends! In that case, maybe I should say that I hope we can often get together and play Mahjong.
I also hope that she can fulfill her dream as soon as possible.
{character:Reina Nanami} Hey, {var:player_nickname}, it's your day off tomorrow!

{character:player} Speaking of A-37... I know it's his day off today, but this morning he was already gone by the time I was ready to leave for work. How can he be even busier than normal on his rest days?
{character:Hinata Takanashi} Oh, Mr. A! He came by in the morning when we'd just opened. He bought some drinks and then left.
{character:player} Oh? What did he buy?
{character:Hinata Takanashi} I didn't really pay attention, though to be fair I rarely see him drink anything but ice water... But, he couldn't have just bought some ice water, could he?
{character:player} I don't think that's very likely. I mean, if he wanted ice water he could have just gone to our fridge! Hmm... There's nothing special added to Éternité's ice water, right...?
Go find Saturne and tell him what you learned yesterday

{character:Reina Nanami} Seems you have really underestimated us, {var:player_nickname}! Éternité has secret recipes for everything, including our ice water! It's just that not many people order it, so I haven't had the chance to tell you.
{character:player} Oh, I'm sorry. I should have warned you I was going to come by. Is it a bad time?
{character:Saturne} No, not at all. It's actually a surprise! Please, come in, my friend.
{character:player} Oh, were you just playing Mahjong?
{character:Saturne} Ahaha! I wouldn't quite say that. I've heard that there's a game that's currently quite popular in One Han City, "Which tile to discard", so I wanted to try it out.

Saturne motions me to sit opposite him. Taking my seat, I notice a Mahjong hand in front of me: 1-Man, 2-Man, 3-Man, 3-Man, 4-Man, 5-Man, 7-Man, 8-Man, 9-Man, 4-Sou, 7-Pin. And the Pair is double 3-Pin. The 9 discarded tiles indicate that it's already the ninth turn.
{character:Saturne} The most fascinating thing about Mahjong is how different people play the same hand.
{character:Saturne} I'm curious how you'd play this, ignoring Round Wind, current points and all that.
Saturne
{character:player} I'd Riichi with the 7-Pin.
{character:Saturne} Can you explain your thinking?

{character:player} Well, looking at the current discards and my hand, I'm in Tenpai waiting for one of five tiles and I've got a good pattern here. Moreover, all the 1-Pin are gone, but not a single 2-Pin has appeared. So maybe they're all still in the wall. If that's the case, I could get 2 Ura Dora if I'm lucky.
{character:Saturne} Haha, so it's like that! I used to think that doing business was a tactical and thrilling battle of wits, but Riichi Mahjong is no less exciting.
{character:player} That it is. If you hadn't said to ignore the points and all that, I think there could have a lot more options too.
{character:Saturne} It's just as I thought! You're talented at this sort of Mahjong. Have you ever considered... Entering a tournament?
{character:player} A tournament?
{character:Saturne} I presume you're calling upon me today because you have some answers to what we discussed before.
{character:Saturne} How interesting... Even the organizers don't remember the rules.
{character:Saturne} As happens, the tournament I just mentioned is precisely this one.
{character:player} How come you know things that even the Mahjong Soul Shrine priestess doesn't?

{character:Saturne} Haha! We businessmen have our own sources. But I suppose it can't hurt to tell you that One Han City has many information brokers. They loiter in the back alleys of the marketplaces, but provide reliable information... If you can afford it.
{character:player} Well, how do THEY know so much about the tournament?
{character:Saturne} Because one of the Four Greats recently got word that the Mahjong Soul Shrine tournament will soon be held once more.
{character:player} Really?! When?!!
{character:Saturne} That is up to her highness, the priestess of the Mahjong Soul Shrine. After all, is she not the true representative of the shrine's master?
{character:Saturne} However, it's hard to imagine such an innocent girl taking on such a heavy burden.
{character:player} I'd like to think she can. Despite her appearance, Ichihime has consistently done well as the Mahjong Soul Shrine priestess.
{character:Saturne} Well... I trust you, and if you vouch for her, then I'll trust her as well.
{character:player} Are you thinking of taking part in the tournament, Saturne?
{character:Saturne} Is that an invitation to play with you?
{character:player} Hmm, I suppose it is. I don't think many people would refuse the chance to take part in a tournament with a friend.

{character:Saturne} Well, I must not let my friend down! Haha, today's shaping up to be a good day—not only have we cleared up some of the mystery surrounding the legend, but we've got an appointment in the diary too.
{character:Saturne} I do believe this calls for a celebration.
{character:player} I'd play the 7-Pin and go for Hidden Tenpai.

{character:player} Currently, the player opposite has discarded 4/5/6 tiles in three consecutive turns, while having made 1 call. Maybe they have already achieved Tenpai, so right now Riichi is risky. What's more, if I can hold out for the 6-Man, that has the potential to improve my hand.
{character:Saturne} Ah, so that's why...
{character:player} Huh?
{character:Saturne} Sorry, I suddenly thought of a friend and got a little distracted.
{character:player} Did the other person also do this "Which tile to discard"?
{character:Saturne} To be honest, he left just before you arrived.

{character:Saturne} He was sitting where you are now, facing the same problem of "Which tile to discard", and actually made the same choice as you. However, this particular friend is a taciturn type, and wouldn't tell me his reasoning no matter how many times I asked. In fact, he even asked me...
{character:Saturne} "Why don't you go for Hidden Tenpai?"
{character:Saturne} That's it. I can't really do a good impression of him, haha.
{character:player} I thought it was quite good! Reminded me of one of my friends, actually.
{character:Saturne} Oh?
{character:player} This friend of mine loves his Hidden Tenpai. He likes to say "Hidden Tenpai is the safest way to play, lurking near the target, waiting for the right moment to strike."
{character:Saturne} Haha! This friend of yours sounds like an interesting character.
{character:player} That reminds me! Is your recent guest the same friend you've been waiting for these past few days?
{character:Saturne} Precisely so! His work keeps him phenomenally busy, so he could only make it today... Although he only stayed a short while before scurrying off again.
{character:player} That's a shame. It's rare to meet someone who thinks the same. How great would it be if we could play a round or two together!

{character:Saturne} We might as well! This friend of mine should be in One Han City for a while longer, though he seems to have his eye on someone, so it might be a little hard to get him on board! But I'm sure we'll find a time to play.
{character:Saturne} Anyway, I presume you're paying me a visit today because you have some answers to what we discussed before, no?

{character:Saturne} I never had any impression of the Four Great Jyanshis, but now that you name them, I realize that they're all pretty important people in One Han City... It's just that they don't often broadcast their status as the Four Greats, so it was hard to connect the dots.

{character:player} That's right! Before I knew Kazuha Saionji, I never would have thought that such a young, beautiful woman would be one of the Four Greats. But, after thinking about it, I don't see why not, as if...
{character:Saturne} As if she was born to be one of the Four Greats!
{character:player} Yeah, that's right.
{character:Saturne} Haha! Well, seeing as we have some clues now, I trust we'll be getting to the bottom of this legend in no time at all.
{character:Saturne} I think some celebration drinks are in order!

{character:Eve Krist} Lily... Wasn't as happy to see me as I thought she would be. I felt... Like she wished I hadn't come looking for her...

{character:Eve Krist} She's different from how she used to be. Mm... It's like she's a totally different person. But, in that first instance when she saw me, I saw the old Lily in her eyes: soft, pure, hopeful.
{character:Eve Krist} Do you think that she has some hidden reason...? I'm sorry, I shouldn't be asking you about this. It's just because, if I can't trust Lily, then who in the whole wide world can?
{character:Eve Krist} Oh, that's right... {var:player_nickname}, there's something I wanted to ask you.
{character:player} Go on?
{character:Eve Krist} I was wondering... Could you teach me Mahjong?

{character:Eve Krist} Because Lily didn't completely reject me! She said that there will soon be a grand Mahjong tournament in One Han City, and that if I beat her in the tournament then she'd come back to Northland with me.
{character:Eve Krist} In Northland, Mahjong's always been a pastime reserved for the church leaders. I never thought that... One day I'd need to know how to play. So... Please...

{character:player} I can tell you how to play, but it's up to you to practice. I can teach you the fundamentals, as well as some basic strategies and tips that I've gained by playing. But where you take this knowledge, and how you grow, is in your hands.

{character:Eve Krist} I do hope that, during my time in One Han City, we can become friends who play Mahjong together, eat together, work together, and play together... Ah, it doesn't really matter what we do, as long as we do it together, {var:player_nickname}!
{character:player} You have my word!
